Multi-scatter GGX compensation. Single-scatter GGX (what sampleBSDF/evalDirectBRDF use) loses energy at high roughness ‚ rough metals/plastics look slightly too dark compared to a real photo. A cheap analytic "furnace test" compensation term (Kulla-Conty style) fixes this for a few ALU ops.

add to path tracer
Firefly clamping / path regularization. No radiance clamp anywhere in the accumulation. Low-roughness specular caustics hit via NEE (or narrow-pdf light-tree picks) can spike hard given 1/pdf divides. A luminance clamp on NEE contributions (or roughness clamping after the first diffuse bounce, PBRT-style) would clean up noise without changing the converged image much.
